To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the local institutional ensemble in Oxfordshire has been successful in attracting and retaining high-tech firms, but that the local system is now in a state of transition as it attempts to adapt to the changing national and international context.
the Oxford Trust and the Oxfordshire Local Enterprise Partnership (OLEP) provide a means of co-ordination of local high-tech firms, local universities and local government.
The Oxford Trust is a unique institution that has developed a range of activities to support the high-tech community in Oxfordshire.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of local innovation systems, and the role of local actors, in shaping local high-tech economic development, and the way in which local innovation systems are shaped by national agendas.
the role of local innovation systems in the context of a national innovation system, and the role of the local trust as a key institution in the local innovation system.
the role of the local in the national and regional innovation systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the local high-tech system in Oxfordshire is a dynamic and complex network of institutions and organisations, which has developed in response to the needs of high-tech firms.
the Oxford case is a good example of the way in which local institutional ensembles can be created to facilitate innovation, and that the Trust is an effective means of doing so.

the local high-tech sector has a high level of institutional capacity and is well placed to respond to national and regional policy initiatives, but that it has not developed the capacity to engage with the wider regional innovation system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
local innovation systems are a complex of institutions and actors that are not only embedded in local networks but are also linked to wider regional and national institutions.

the local innovation system is not simply a set of institutions and networks, but a set of discourses which provide the means by which local interests are articulated and which shape the development of local innovation systems.
the Oxford Trust and its networks provide a means of linking local innovation systems to the wider regional innovation system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of local innovation systems is contingent upon the development of institutional capacity.
the development of innovation ensembles depends on the capacity to develop local networks of trust and the ability of local institutions to represent local interests in wider arenas.
innovation systems are not static.
